description:
FILED s451x (Opus agent X), hit while writing the #542 guard file: a gate row
that called tempfile() inside the TRANSPILED program aborted, so the row had
to be rewritten to build its scratch path from $$ instead.

REPRO:

    use File::Temp qw(tempfile);
    my (undef, $f) = tempfile(OPEN => 0);
    print "got $f\n";

        perl  got /tmp/XXXXXXXXXX-ish name
        PCL   Error in tempfile() using template /tmp/XXXXXXXXXX: The template
              must end with at least 4 'X' characters   (fatal, via Carp)

The template it names ENDS WITH TEN 'X', so the shim's own check is what is
wrong -- most likely it tests the template before the directory is joined on,
or after, in the wrong order, or it tests the joined path with a regex
anchored somewhere it should not be.  Layer: lib/File/Temp.pm (CLAUDE.md 9a --
this is one module's behaviour), unless the check is really a PCL regex/anchor
bug, which the probe will say.

BAR: the repro plus the OPEN=>1 default spelling and an explicit TEMPLATE, all
against the perl oracle; then restore the tempfile() spelling in
Pl/t/stdio-buffering-01.t's row 7 (it carries a pointer to this task).

CLOSED s451z -- and the PROBE said COMPILER, not shim, exactly as the task
allowed for.  The shim's check is fine; what was wrong is that a file's own
`use constant` is invisible to a named sub's BODY, which is lowered before the
in-stream statement registers the name.  So

    use constant MINX => 4;
    substr($template, $start - MINX + 1, MINX)

emitted `(p-substr $template (p-- $start (pl-MINX 1 (pl-MINX))))` -- MINX
swallowed `+ 1, MINX` as ARGUMENTS, substr got TWO arguments, and it answered
5 characters where perl gives 4.  Minimal repro (no module needed):

    use constant K => 4;
    sub p { my ($s,$i)=@_; substr($s, $i - K + 1, K) }
    print p("/tmp/XXXXXXXXXX", 14);     perl [XXXX]   PCL [XXXXX]

FIX: `Parser2::_premerge_use_constant_prototypes`, beside the pre-pass that
already does this for the `*NAME = sub () {â¦}` idiom; the NAMES come from ONE
reader (`Pl::Parser::use_constant_names`, both spellings) and the RECORD from
ONE writer (`Pl::Parser::register_constant_prototype`, which the emitter now
calls too).

MEASURED: `tempfile(OPEN => 0)` bare / with a leading TEMPLATE / with DIR /
with SUFFIX all identical to perl.  corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111 files.
Guard `Pl/t/imported-term-01.t` 11 -> 15 rows (the sub body, the hash form, and
two inverses: top level was already right, and a PLAIN sub of the same shape
must keep taking arguments).

NOT DONE, and it cannot be: restoring `tempfile()` in
Pl/t/stdio-buffering-01.t row 7.  The DEFAULT spelling needs a handle and
`sysopen` is not implemented -- a second, unrelated failure, filed as #730.
The row keeps its $$ path and its comment now says so.
